procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rescheduled from Dec no-show. Doing ok. Holidays were rough on routine; admits he missed a stretch of the HIV pill over Christmas week, back on it now. ID visit was in early December per him.

Diet: a lot of takeout. Not checking sugars.
Still ~10 cig/day.

Vitals as charted. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No edema. Feet look fine.

A/P: DM2 - A1c, BMP. HTN - continue lisinopril 20. CKD 3a - recheck creatinine. HIV - urged him to call ID if he runs short of pills rather than going without. Smoking - he asked about vaping instead; told him that is not the answer I'd pick but quitting is. RTC 3-4 mo.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c crept up a little to the low 7s. Kidney number 1.7, about the same range as last year. Let's work on the food side before adding anything. Metformin as before.

documents.title: Refill: metformin, lisinopril
documents.author: MA
documents.body: eRx refill request from pharmacy for metformin 1000 mg #180 and lisinopril 20 mg #90. Last seen 1/10, labs current. Sent per protocol, PCP cosign.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, he's at home, partner in the background. Wanted to touch base instead of coming in - ride issues again.

Taking metformin and lisinopril. HIV pill "better than winter", maybe 5 of 7 days. Partner reminds him. No fevers, rashes, cough, diarrhea. No dark urine, no leg swelling.

No vitals today.

Plan: no changes. Bring him in for labs with the physical in September. Asked him to keep his ID appointment in June.

documents.title: Infectious Disease Follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
ID clinic visit 06/13/2022.

HIV-1 on bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF with TMP-SMX DS prophylaxis. Missed the March visit. By pill count he has taken roughly two thirds of doses since the winter.

CD4 190. HIV-1 RNA 15,000 copies/mL, up from 1,200 a year ago.

No opportunistic symptoms. Exam: afebrile, no thrush, no lymphadenopathy, skin clear.

Assessment: viremia from incomplete adherence; no reason to suspect resistance yet, genotype sent.
Plan: same regimen. Linked with our case manager for transportation and pharmacy delivery. Continue TMP-SMX. Return 3 months.

Allergies: none known.

documents.title: Diabetic Eye Examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Dilated eye exam 08/24/2022 for diabetes.
Visual acuity 20/20 right, 20/25 left. Pressures normal.
Fundus: no hemorrhages, microaneurysms or exudates either eye. Discs healthy.
Assessment: no diabetic retinopathy. Return one year.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Turning 35 next month.

Interval: ID in June, viral load went up because of missed doses; they set him up with a case manager and pharmacy delivery, which he says helps. Taking the pill "most days" now. No hospital or ER visits. Eye doctor in August, no retinopathy.

ROS: no fevers, sweats, weight change, cough, dysphagia, diarrhea, rash, headache. No dark urine. No swelling. Sexual health: one partner.
PHQ-9 5 - some stress about money, no SI.
Smoking unchanged.

Exam: vitals as charted. Oral mucosa moist, no thrush or leukoplakia. No cervical or axillary nodes. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Skin intact, no lesions. Ext no edema. Feet: monofilament intact, pulses good, no calluses.

A/P
1. Health maintenance - flu and bivalent COVID booster today. Tdap and PCV20 done last year. Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, UA, urine microalbumin.
2. CKD 3a with albuminuria - brought nephrology up again; he would still rather not. Will keep pressing.
3. HIV - per ID.
4. DM2, HTN - continue current.
RTC Jan.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Andre, labs are mostly steady. Urine protein is higher than last year (610). Kidney function itself is holding. This is the part I'd really like a kidney doctor to see - the offer stands any time, just tell me and we'll set it up.

documents.title: RE: Physical labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: ok. after the new year maybe. thanks

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u DM2, HTN, CKD 3a, HIV.

No complaints. Not interested in nephrology yet ("after the new year" has become "in the spring").
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, ART + TMP-SMX per ID - adherence by report maybe 70-80%.

Exam: as charted. RRR. Clear lungs. No edema.

Plan: BMP, A1c. Continue meds. Spring visit by video if transport is still a problem.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit from his kitchen. Feels fine. No dark urine or swelling. Says he has ID in two weeks. Taking metformin and lisinopril daily; ART "most days".

No vitals.

Refills sent. Nephrology - he said ask again in the summer. Noted. Labs at next in-person visit.

documents.title: Infectious Disease Follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Seen 05/22/2023. HIV-1 on bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF and daily TMP-SMX DS.

Adherence remains poor; refill records show gaps of 1-3 weeks. He is frank that some weeks he just does not take it. No opportunistic symptoms.

CD4 175. HIV-1 RNA 38,000 copies/mL. Prior genotype without major resistance mutations.

Exam: afebrile, oropharynx clear, no nodes, lungs clear, skin without lesions.

Plan: same regimen; motivational counseling with our social worker; weekly blister packs from the delivery pharmacy. Continue prophylaxis. Return 3 months.

Allergies: NKDA.

orders.reason: Dark urine after URI with known proteinuria and hematuria, CKD 3a

documents.title: pee is dark
documents.author: patient
documents.body: sorry its sunday. since yesterday my pee is like brown, like coke. little ache in my side/back. i had a cold that went away about a week ago. no burning. should i go to the ER

documents.title: RE: pee is dark
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad you wrote. No fever, vomiting or severe pain? If any of those, go to the ER. Otherwise I'd like you seen by the kidney specialists tomorrow - this is exactly the reason I've wanted them involved. I'm messaging the nephrology on-call now to get you a slot Monday. Drink normally, no ibuprofen or similar.

documents.title: RE: RE: pee is dark
documents.author: patient
documents.body: no fever no throwing up. ok ill go tomorrow

documents.title: Nephrology urgent slot
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with nephrology on call. They will see him tomorrow at 2:30 in clinic. Texted pt the time and address. Faxing last 2 yrs of labs in the morning.

documents.title: Nephrology Consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEPHROLOGY GROUP - CONSULTATION
Seen 07/17/2023 at the request of primary care.

CC: dark urine x 2 days.

HPI: 35-year-old man with HIV, type 2 diabetes, hypertension and CKD stage 3a with longstanding albuminuria and microscopic hematuria. He had an upper respiratory infection that cleared about a week ago; two days ago his urine turned dark and he has had a mild ache in the flank. On questioning he recalls a few similar spells over roughly the last three years, each after a cold, each clearing on its own; he never reported them. No NSAIDs or other new medications, no dysuria, no rash, no joint complaints.

Meds: lisinopril 20 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg BID, bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF daily, TMP-SMX DS daily (ID).
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: mother with type 2 diabetes, father hypertension, a maternal uncle on dialysis (cause not known).
Social: smokes about 10 cigarettes a day; occasional alcohol; not working, previously in security.

Exam: BP 152/96. Comfortable. No rash, no joint swelling, no edema. No CVA tenderness to speak of.

Data: urinalysis with red cell casts on microscopy and proteinuria. Creatinine 1.8 (his baseline in your records 1.5-1.7). Serum albumin 3.9. 24-hour urine protein 2.1 g/day.

Impression: episodes of gross hematuria arriving a few days after upper respiratory infections, on a background of persistent microscopic hematuria and proteinuria, with active sediment - most consistent with IgA nephropathy. Albumin is preserved; not nephrotic.
Plan:
- Continue lisinopril.
- Repeat creatinine and urine protein in 4-6 weeks.
- Kidney biopsy if proteinuria rises or function declines.
- Avoid NSAIDs.
- Return in 6 months, sooner as needed.

Thank you for this referral.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Back after nephrology. Urine went back to normal color within about 4 days. No flank pain now.

Read the nephrology letter with him: IgA nephropathy is their working diagnosis, biopsy if it gets worse. He's relieved there's a name for it. Plans to keep the 6-month nephrology appointment.

BP high again today. He says it's always up here. Lisinopril 20 continued as is.

Exam: RRR, lungs clear, no edema.

Labs today: CMP, CBC, UA, A1c (repeat requested by nephrology, results to them).
Updated problem list. RTC Oct for flu shot, Jan after nephrology.

documents.title: Labs faxed to nephrology
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Faxed 8/14 CMP, CBC, UA to nephrology per their request. Confirmation received. Pt left vm that his urine is still clear.

documents.title: Diabetic Eye Examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Annual diabetic eye exam 09/13/2023, dilated.
Acuity 20/20 OD, 20/20 OS with current glasses. Normal pressures.
Retina: no diabetic changes either eye. Macula flat. Optic nerves normal.
No retinopathy. Recall in 12 months.

documents.title: Influenza vaccination
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. Screening questions negative. Declined updated COVID today, wants to wait. Tolerated well.

documents.title: ankles
documents.author: patient
documents.body: my ankles have been puffy for about 2 weeks, worse at night. pee is foamy sometimes. not dark tho. kidney appt is january 8. is that ok or should i come in

documents.title: RE: ankles
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me. Any shortness of breath, chest pain, or swelling going up above the knees? If no, keep the Jan 8 visit, I'll send nephrology a note so they know. Put your feet up in the evening and go light on salt. If it's getting worse fast, message me and I'll see you this week.

documents.title: RE: RE: ankles
documents.author: patient
documents.body: no to all of that. ok
